subject: ventures/quick-pick-survey
professional: a survey methodologist / psychometrician who builds preference and choice-modelling studies (paired comparison, conjoint): first checks that the rating update and the pooled interval are the published formulas, then whether the stated uncertainty is honest and whether the tests would notice if it were not

evidence.correctness: Ran the modules with tsx and recomputed with a separate Python implementation written from Glickman's 2012 Glicko-2 paper (not from the repo code). (1) 1500/RD200/vol0.06 beats 1400/RD30: tool 1563.564, RD 175.403, vol 0.0599987; Python identical to 6 d.p. (2) same player loses to 1550/RD100: 1426.686 / 175.903 / 0.0599990; identical. (3) fresh 1500/350 pair, A wins: 1662.311 and 1337.689, RD 290.319; identical; an EQUAL result leaves both at exactly 1500, RD 290.319, as it must. (4) DerSimonian-Laird pool of (1600,rd100),(1400,rd100),(1550,rd80): tool rating 1521.347, se 56.006, tau 30.773; Python from the DL formulas gave the same; a homogeneous set (1600/100,1580/120,1590/90) gives tau 0, rating 1591.043, se 58.430, also identical. All recomputed outputs agree. Not recomputed: the Davidson/Bradley-Terry Newton-Raphson fit (conjoint.ts), pair selection, couples comparison. Departure: the pooled interval treats each respondent's Glicko RD as a sampling standard error (see domain).
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: per-respondent Glicko-2 for discrete items (works, tested); admin survey builder and pooled ranking with 95% interval, rank range, CSV (groupRanking.ts and surveyBuilder.ts run, unit tests pass); Davidson/Bradley-Terry for continuous attributes (conjoint.ts present with tests); three perspectives and couples comparison (couples.ts, perspective.ts, tests pass); sample report page (site/ present, script in scripts/build-sample-report.mjs, not regenerated). NOT run end to end: the Next.js app, `npm run build`, typecheck, lint, the integration suite (needs a real Postgres; none started here) and the Vercel one-click deploy. README itself says CI 'has never actually run'. VENTURE.yaml stage is prototype, no production URL, no external user. Features that work in unit tests but were not exercised in a running app are scored as unverified, hence 2.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/quick-pick-survey && npm ci --ignore-scripts && npx prisma generate && npx vitest run --config vitest.fast.config.ts: 35 files, 298 tests, 298 pass (the simulation and integration suites were not run: simulations are minutes long, integrations need Postgres). Without prisma generate couples.test.ts fails to load, so 261 tests passed and 1 file failed until generate ran. Seeded four mutations, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean): (a) groupRanking.ts:52 DL numerator (q - (k - 1)) changed to (q - k): groupRanking and surveyBuilder tests 20/20 still pass, NOT caught; (b) groupRanking.ts:39 Z95 1.96 changed to 1.64, so every published 95% interval is 16% too narrow: groupRanking.test.ts 12/12 pass, NOT caught; (c) glicko2.ts:14 MIN_RD 30 changed to 20: full fast suite 298/298 pass, NOT caught; (d) glicko2.ts:13 TAU 0.5 changed to 1.2: glicko2.test.ts 11/11 pass, NOT caught. Tests check direction and ordering (tau > 200 for a split panel, tau == 0 for agreement) but never an exact interval, rating or tau, so a wrong statistical constant ships green. Score 2: good breadth, but zero of four core-logic mutations detected.
evidence.craft: Read glicko2.ts, groupRanking.ts, conjoint.ts (first 120 lines), rateLimit.ts, plus the repo layout (decisions/ADRs, integration-test harness, route inventory tests, typed development-process file guarded by a test). Clean typed modules, log-space softmax in the Davidson model, ridge prior with the reason written down, convergence on per-row gradient with the reason written down, CSV formula-injection guard (FORMULA_LEAD in groupRanking.ts:98). Defects: the group-ranking CI uses 1.96 normal quantiles with no small-k correction (k=2 or 3 respondents per item is allowed; THIN_RESPONDENTS is 3); updateGlicko's volatility loop `while (f(a - k*TAU) < 0) k++` has no iteration cap; Hessian is finite-difference. Nothing copied or dead found in the files read; no TODO/FIXME in src.
evidence.claims: README and llms.txt claims checked: Glicko-2 per respondent (glicko2.ts, matches), random-effects pooling that widens with disagreement (groupRanking.ts, verified numerically: tau 30.8 widened se vs fixed-effect), Davidson tie model (conjoint.ts header formulas are the standard form), 'CI has never run' (honest, backed by IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md P1), disclaimer present in README, site/index.html and the report page, 'price is a guess nobody has tested' on the report page (candid). Unbacked or stale: llms.txt:9 links the live page at duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/quick-pick-survey/ although the README and the repo say the address is marisstella.app and GitHub Pages only redirects; llms.txt:10 source link uses lowercase 'duncan-haywood' while the README links Duncan-Haywood (works, inconsistent). README says 'including trade-offs you couldn't state directly' and 'knows your preference ordering' with no accuracy figure for the real-user case; docs/CONVERGENCE.md measures it on simulation only (not re-run). The headline 'confidence interval' is described as '95%' although mutation (b) shows no test pins that number.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a small team lead who wants to rank 10 options with colleagues: deploy needs a Vercel account, a Postgres, two secrets and `prisma migrate deploy`; the admin builds a survey from pasted lines (API or admin page), shares /s/<slug>, respondents answer pairs, GET /ranking returns ranks with ranges and CSV. The design answers the job well (rank ranges instead of false ties, thin-coverage advice). I could not complete the walk-through: no database, no running app, no browser. Limits a user hits: self-hosted only, no hosted instance, no consent or sampling tooling (llms.txt says so), no external user ever (kill criterion untested). Prototype stage.
evidence.domain: Compared against Bradley-Terry/Thurstone paired-comparison practice and Glickman 2012. Sound: Glicko-2 matches the paper exactly on single-game periods; per-respondent state so individuals are not mixed; random-effects pooling with DerSimonian-Laird (Biostatistics standard); Davidson ties; ridge prior stated; decisions record why pooling across perspectives was rejected. Departures a psychometrician would flag: (1) Glicko-2 is an online rating system whose result depends on question order and volatility updates, a Bradley-Terry fit on all of a respondent's answers is the usual survey estimator and gives order-invariant estimates; (2) a Glicko RD is a posterior spread under the model, not a sampling standard error, so feeding it into DL as v_i and calling the result a '95% interval' is a heuristic (the docs do not say so plainly); (3) MIN_RD 30 and unspecified small-sample behaviour mean intervals can look tighter than 3 respondents justify; (4) the 'trade-offs they couldn't state' claim rests on a conjoint model with a ridge prior, whose identifiability with 10 to 20 answers is simulated, not validated on humans.

defects.what: Pooled 95% intervals and tau are unpinned by tests: changing Z95 from 1.96 to 1.64 and the DL numerator (q-(k-1)) to (q-k) left all tests green, so a wrong interval would ship
Glicko-2 constants (MIN_RD floor 30, system constant TAU) are untested: MIN_RD 30 to 20 passes the whole 298-test fast suite, TAU 0.5 to 1.2 passes glicko2.test.ts

Each respondent's Glicko RD is used as a sampling standard error in a random-effects meta-analysis and the output is labelled a 95% interval, with a normal quantile and as few as 2 to 3 raters per item; the limits are not stated next to the interval
llms.txt points the live page at the retired github.io host instead of https://marisstella.app/quick-pick-survey/

couples.test.ts imports @prisma/client at load, so the 'fast, needs nothing running' unit suite fails to load on a fresh checkout until `prisma generate` runs (npm ci --ignore-scripts, or postinstall blocked)

verdict: The arithmetic is right: four Glicko-2 updates and two DerSimonian-Laird pools recompute to 6 decimal places against an independent Python implementation, the code is clean and the docs are unusually candid (CI never ran, price untested, disclaimer everywhere). It does not meet the bar because 298 of 298 passing tests did not catch any of four seeded changes to the core statistics (the 1.96 quantile, the DL formula, the rating floor, the volatility constant), so the headline 95% interval is correct today by luck of the author's care rather than by a test; the app, build, typecheck and integration suite were not run here, and a methodologist would object to treating a Glicko RD as a sampling error and to an order-dependent online estimator for a survey. It is a well-built prototype with no external user yet, not a tool a practitioner would sign off on.
